item.title: Real Madrid seek Super League setup payments from Premier League six
item.description: Real Madrid are seeking contributions towards the setup costs of the failed European Super League project from the six Premier League clubs that withdrew shortly after its launch, the Spanish side confirmed to Reuters on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Kallas
item.content:encoded: Real Madrid are seeking contributions towards the setup costs of the failed European Super League project from the six Premier League clubs that withdrew shortly after its launch, the Spanish side confirmed to Reuters on Tuesday. The Athletic reported that the total costs could reach €80 million ($89.9 million). Real are seeking payments from Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur. The six were among nine of the competition's 12 founding clubs that withdrew within three days of its launch in 2021 amid widespread opposition. Real did not immediately confirm whether they were also seeking payments from the other three early leavers, AC Milan, Inter Milan and Atletico Madrid. Real Madrid said the six English clubs were liable for costs incurred in establishing the competition, which have so far been covered by Juventus, Barcelona and Real. Tottenham declined to comment while the other five Premier League clubs did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. The Athletic reported that the clubs signed a shareholders' agreement for the European Super League Company, the holding company behind the competition, although it is unclear whether the contract explicitly set out their liability for setup costs. The Super League collapsed shortly after its launch following the withdrawal of the nine clubs. Juventus subsequently pulled out of the project and Barcelona formally withdrew in February, leaving Real Madrid as its sole remaining founding club. Real, UEFA and European Football Clubs announced an agreement of principles on February 11 aimed at resolving their Super League-related legal disputes. ($1 = 0.8903 euros)

item.title: Anthropic recorded net loss of over $80 billion in first half of this year, WSJ reports
item.description: AI startup Anthropic recorded a net loss of more than $80 billion in the first half of this year, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing a draft initial public offering prospectus.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: AI startup Anthropic recorded a net loss of more than $80 billion in the first half of this year, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing a draft initial public offering prospectus. That compares to a net loss of $13 billion during the same period a year earlier, according to the report. The vast majority of that loss, $72 billion, resulted from accounting charges tied to changes in the value of convertible notes and other instruments the company issued to raise funding, the Journal report said. Anthropic did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

item.title: Dados do TSE indicam aumento, e não redução de seções eleitorais em 2026
item.description: Dados públicos do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) mostram aumento do número de seções eleitorais em 2026 na comparação com pleitos anteriores, ao contrário do que afirmam publicações nas redes sociais.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Dados públicos do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) mostram aumento do número de seções eleitorais em 2026 na comparação com pleitos anteriores, ao contrário do que afirmam publicações nas redes sociais. Estes são os principais detalhes: Um vídeo que circula no Facebook e Instagram afirma que o TSE diminuiu a quantidade de seções eleitorais. “No ano de 2022, tínhamos 500.300 urnas. No ano de 2026, nós tivemos 499.200”, diz o autor do conteúdo. O vídeo mostra o número de 500.341 seções. No entanto, esse total não se refere a 2022, mas à soma das seções da eleição municipal de 2024 , o que inclui seções agregadas às principais ou que não foram instaladas. O autor do vídeo acaba comparando as seções de 2024 ao total de seções principais deste ano (499.248). O total de seções de 2026, incluindo as agregadas e não instaladas, é de 517.179. As seções principais podem receber eleitores de outras (agregadas). As seções instaladas são as principais que estão de fato prontas para os eleitores votarem. O site do TSE mostra que o primeiro turno da eleição deste ano teve 499.207 seções instaladas. Em 2022 , foram 472.028 instaladas. O autor do vídeo afirmou que o TSE alterou os dados depois da publicação do post. Veredicto: Falso. Dados do TSE indicam que houve aumento no número de seções instaladas em 2026 na comparação com eleições anteriores. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

item.title: FAA certifies Boeing's 737 MAX 10, clearing way for deliveries
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration on Tuesday granted final approval to the long-delayed Boeing 737 MAX 10, clearing the way for the US planemaker to begin delivering the largest version of it best-selling airplane.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Federal Aviation Administration on Tuesday granted final approval to the long-delayed Boeing (BA.N) 737 MAX 10, clearing the way for the US planemaker to begin delivering the largest version of it best-selling airplane. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is set to appear on Tuesday at a Boeing factory in Everett, Washington, to tout the FAA certification. Boeing in July opened a new production line at the Everett plant to increase 737 output, which it also assembles in Renton. Before the delays, Boeing had initially planned to start delivering the MAX 10 in 2020.

item.title: Brent cai enquanto presidente do Irã discute mediação com chefe do Exército do Paquistão
item.description: Os preços do petróleo fecharam em queda após atingirem a maior cotação em cinco meses nesta terça-feira, enquanto os operadores avaliavam um encontro entre o presidente iraniano e o chefe do Exército do Paquistão — um importante mediador entre os Estados Unidos e o Irã —, em contraste com os contínuos ataques houthis à infraestrutura saudita e relatos de ataques a embarcações no Golfo.
item.dc:creator: Georgina Mccartney
item.content:encoded: Os preços do petróleo fecharam em queda após atingirem a maior cotação em cinco meses nesta terça-feira, enquanto os operadores avaliavam um encontro entre o presidente iraniano e o chefe do Exército do Paquistão — um importante mediador entre os Estados Unidos e o Irã —, em contraste com os contínuos ataques houthis à infraestrutura saudita e relatos de ataques a embarcações no Golfo. Os futuros do petróleo Brent fecharam em queda de 0,69%, a US$108,79. No início do pregão, o contrato com vencimento mais próximo atingiu US$111,99, a maior cotação em cinco meses. O contrato de novembro do petróleo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dos EUA, que venceu nesta terça-feira, fechou com queda de US$1,87, ou 1,8%, a US$101,79. Esse valor ficou abaixo da máxima do pregão, de US$110,48, a maior cotação desde abril para um contrato de vencimento próximo. O contrato de dezembro, mais ativo, fechou com queda de 72 centavos, a US$97,82 o barril. O presidente do Irã, Masoud Pezeshkian, discutiu os esforços de mediação e os desdobramentos regionais durante uma reunião com o chefe do Exército do Paquistão, o marechal de campo Asim Munir, em Teerã, informou a agência iraniana Nournews nesta terça-feira. Os esforços de mediação do Paquistão resultaram em um acordo de paz provisório assinado em junho. Mas esse acordo rapidamente fracassou em meio a novos confrontos entre o Irã e os EUA semanas depois. As negociações em Teerã ocorrem em um contexto de ataques contínuos por parte dos houthis do Iêmen, alinhados ao Irã, que afirmaram na segunda-feira ter lançado vários ataques contra alvos energéticos, aeroportuários e militares da Arábia Saudita, como uma instalação da Aramco (2222.SE) em Yanbu, o campo petrolífero de Shaybah, o Aeroporto Internacional Rei Khalid, em Riade, e o aeroporto de Abha. As autoridades sauditas não confirmaram imediatamente as alegações dos houthis, e a Reuters não conseguiu verificá-las de forma independente. “Os preços do petróleo continuam bem sustentados... Isso sugere que o mercado está precificando um prêmio de risco significativo, dada a volatilidade da situação”, afirmaram analistas do ING em uma nota nesta terça-feira. Pelo menos 18 embarcações teriam sido atacadas ao longo de duas semanas, o que mantém o prêmio de risco intacto, informou a empresa de rastreamento de navios Kpler em uma nota na segunda-feira. Também na segunda-feira, um ataque houthi a um campo de treinamento das forças de segurança do governo na província de Shabwa, no Iêmen, matou 58 pessoas e feriu mais de 200. A retomada dos ataques intensificou os temores quanto à estabilidade regional e ressaltou os riscos contínuos ao abastecimento de energia proveniente da região, mantendo os preços do petróleo acima de US$100 por barril. O primeiro-ministro israelense, Benjamin Netanyahu, afirmou em comunicado que está “comprometido em concluir a eliminação do regime iraniano” e conversou com o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, sobre o assunto no domingo.

item.title: Citi México ve nuevas oportunidades con bancos tras escisión de Banamex
item.description: La filial mexicana de Citigroup busca expandir su negocio con otros bancos después de que su separación de Banamex le otorgara mayor libertad para prestar servicios a instituciones financieras, dijo el martes a Reuters Luis Brossier, consejero delegado de Citi México.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Araujo
item.content:encoded: La filial mexicana de Citigroup busca expandir su negocio con otros bancos después de que su separación de Banamex le otorgara mayor libertad para prestar servicios a instituciones financieras, dijo el martes a Reuters Luis Brossier, consejero delegado de Citi México. Citi separó Banamex de su negocio de banca institucional en 2024, como parte de un plan más amplio para deshacerse de su participación en el banco minorista, lo que pretende hacer por completo a través de una oferta pública inicial prevista para 2027. Brossier afirmó que la separación ha permitido a Citi México operar de manera más similar al negocio corporativo de Citi en mercados como Brasil, donde la banca de inversión, los mercados y los servicios transaccionales han impulsado el crecimiento. "Es que los clientes ya los teníamos porque al final el negocio corporativo nos lo trajimos de Banamex", dijo Brossier en una entrevista en São Paulo. "La oportunidad ahora radica en cómo podemos ofrecer más a esos mismos clientes". Según explicó, una vía de crecimiento consiste en ofrecer servicios a otros bancos, un negocio que Citi no pudo desarrollar de forma agresiva mientras fue propietaria de Banamex. "Citi en el mundo tiende a ser un banco de bancos", dijo Brossier, haciendo referencia a la presencia internacional y la infraestructura financiera de la entidad. Este cambio ya está dando resultados, añadió Brossier, y Banamex está a punto de convertirse en un cliente importante. Recientemente, Citi lideró la emisión adicional de bonos de nivel uno de Banamex, la primera venta de deuda de alto riesgo del banco minorista en su proceso de consolidación de un balance independiente tras su separación de Citi. Citi también participará en la eventual salida a bolsa de Banamex. Brossier también hizo referencia a su relación comercial con BBVA (BBVA.MC) en México, afirmando que Citi ha gestionado emisiones de bonos para el banco, un trabajo que, según él, habría sido improbable cuando Banamex todavía formaba parte de Citi. Citi también ve oportunidades para expandir su segmento de banca comercial, que presta servicios a empresas medianas, así como su división de banca privada. Según explicó, la estrategia refleja el enfoque de Citi en Brasil, donde la banca comercial incorpora a empresas de rápido crecimiento a su red con el objetivo de convertirlas en clientes institucionales de mayor envergadura. "Se trata de captación de clientes", dijo Brossier refiriéndose a la banca comercial en México. "El resto del negocio, sin duda, es cómo hacemos más para los mismos clientes que ya tenemos".

item.title: Stars D Esa Lindell (lower body) out at least a week
item.description: Dallas Stars defenseman Esa Lindell will miss at least a week because of a lower-body injury, coach Glen Gulutzan said Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Dallas Stars defenseman Esa Lindell will miss at least a week because of a lower-body injury, coach Glen Gulutzan said Tuesday. Lindell, 32, was injured blocking a shot in the Stars' 4-0 road victory over the Chicago Blackhawks on Saturday. "Esa is going to be out here for a bit," Gulutzan said. "I would say right now probably for a week for sure and then we'll go day to day after that." Lindell has no points in eight games with a plus-4 rating, two penalty minutes, 18 blocks and four hits. He tied a career high with 32 points and set a new mark with 26 assists in 2025-26, when he played in all 82 games for the third time in four seasons. Lindell played in 80 games in 2024-25. For his career, Lindell has 249 points (60 goals, 189 assists), a plus-172 rating, 180 penalty minutes, 1,467 blocks and 892 hits in 774 regular-season games since the 2015-16 campaign. He also has 25 points (six goals, 19 assists) in 109 playoff games. Dallas selected the native of Finland in the third round of the 2012 NHL Draft. --Field Level Media

item.title: Trump dice que Ucrania tiene que querer poner fin a la guerra
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, instó el martes a Ucrania a llegar a un acuerdo para poner fin a la guerra con Rusia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, instó el martes a Ucrania a llegar a un acuerdo para poner fin a la guerra con Rusia. "Ucrania tiene que querer poner fin a esta guerra", dijo Trump a periodistas en el Despacho Oval. El enviado de Trump, Steve Witkoff, se encontraba el martes en Oslo, para mantener conversaciones con el presidente de Ucrania, Volodímir Zelenski, con el objetivo de poner fin a la invasión rusa de Ucrania, que ya dura cuatro años. Trump sugirió que Moscú llevaba la ventaja en el conflicto porque "Rusia es una gran máquina: simplemente siguen avanzando sin descanso, y eso es lo que han hecho. Han tomado un pedazo de territorio muy grande".

item.title: Bavuma battles adversity to put South Africa in control
item.description: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma said he enjoyed battling against adversity as he scored 179 on Tuesday to turn around his side’s fortunes in the second test against Australia and also quell some of his own mental demons.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma said he enjoyed battling against adversity as he scored 179 on Tuesday to turn around his side’s fortunes in the second test against Australia and also quell some of his own mental demons. The captain produced a defiant display and showcased his batting skills as South Africa recovered from a precarious 110-6 in the morning session on the third day to declare on 425-9 before taking an Australian wicket prior to stumps, an emphatic response to their heavy defeat in last week’s first test. The 36-year-old Bavuma had been forced to the crease with the hosts on 12-2 on Sunday’s rain-restricted opening day, when only an hour's play was possible, and had to resume his innings on Monday as the ball moved around after the wet weather finally relented. South Africa slumped to 97-5 by the close of the second day. “I walked into a tricky situation,” he told reporters. “I think everything was in the bowlers’ favour, the conditions overhead, the wicket itself, we’d just lost two early wickets, but ordinarily I’ve found myself in those situations quite a number of times and I guess it seems to bring out the best in me." The sun appeared on Tuesday after two rain-affected days and the pitch flattened out, offering the batters considerably more assistance, although Bavuma insisted conditions were not as easy as they might have seemed. DEALING WITH AUSTRALIA’S QUALITY ATTACK “With the quality of the bowling attack, they're still able to put you under pressure, even when the ball is slightly softer and older. “I think from a mindset point of view, for me, nothing really changed. I was always just trying to be as tight as I could and try to hit the ball as straight as I could. “The one thing was being able to get the team out of a tough situation. But then from a personal point of view, to go on to getting a big 100, that's obviously something that's been a thorn in my side throughout my career. So it was nice to get over that mental hurdle,” he added. Bavuma, who has overcome a long-standing elbow injury, not only surpassed his previous highest test score but featured in two record partnerships. He added 132 with Marco Jansen, who scored 85, to set a South African seventh-wicket record at St George’s Park, before putting on a national-record 183 for the eighth wicket with number nine Simon Harmer, who made a test career-best 82. “They put a heavy price on their wickets and part of our plan was to keep Australia in the field for as long as we could. It all went according to plan,” Bavuma added as Australia will resume at 3–1 at the start of day four.

item.title: Para Lula, la soberanía de Brasil está en juego en la última vuelta de las elecciones
item.description: Cuando Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se dirigió a la Asamblea General de la ONU el mes pasado, aprovechó uno de los escenarios diplomáticos más importantes del mundo para transmitir un mensaje que ha llegado a definir la que probablemente sea la última campaña presidencial de su carrera de varias décadas.
item.dc:creator: Brendan O'Boyle, Lisandra Paraguassu
item.content:encoded: Cuando Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se dirigió a la Asamblea General de la ONU el mes pasado, aprovechó uno de los escenarios diplomáticos más importantes del mundo para transmitir un mensaje que ha llegado a definir la que probablemente sea la última campaña presidencial de su carrera de varias décadas. "Brasil no cabe en el patio trasero de nadie", afirmó, en una indirecta velada al Gobierno del presidente estadounidense Donald Trump, que, en su opinión, está poniendo en tela de juicio la soberanía de Brasil. Lula ha presentado las elecciones brasileñas como parte de una batalla más amplia contra las fuerzas antidemocráticas, advirtiendo de la "injerencia extranjera" en una contienda que concluye el domingo con una reñida segunda vuelta frente al senador de derecha Flavio Bolsonaro. En el primer debate entre los candidatos, celebrado días antes de las elecciones, Lula acusó a la familia Bolsonaro, encabezada por el expresidente Jair Bolsonaro, de estar "subordinada a los intereses estadounidenses". Señaló las reuniones celebradas entre los Bolsonaro y Trump a principios de este año, antes de que este último impusiera nuevos aranceles a los productos brasileños. En julio, Lula afirmó que los nuevos aranceles eran el resultado de una "conspiración" con los Bolsonaro "impulsada por objetivos electorales". El año pasado, el hermano del senador, Eduardo Bolsonaro, que vive en Estados Unidos, describió los aranceles de Trump sobre la carne de vacuno, el café, el pescado, el calzado y otros productos brasileños como una "medicina amarga" destinada a frenar lo que él denominó una ofensiva legal descontrolada contra su padre. "La presión que ejercieron para que Estados Unidos impusiera aranceles a Brasil y su deseo de que Brasil sufriera algún perjuicio", afirmó Lula en el debate. "El hermano está allí incitando a un golpe de Estado contra Brasil". La familia desmintió las acusaciones. El Departamento de Estado también ha desmentido cargos anteriores de injerencia electoral. CAMINO DIFÍCIL A LA VICTORIA La primera vuelta de las elecciones puso de manifiesto los límites del mensaje de Lula. Más del 47% de los votantes respaldó a Bolsonaro, un aliado declarado de Trump, que se situó casi dos puntos porcentuales por delante del líder de izquierda. Lula llega a los últimos días de campaña en las encuestas ligeramente por detrás de Bolsonaro, cuyo padre cumple una condena de 27 años por planear un golpe de Estado fallido contra la victoria electoral de Lula en 2022. Aunque Lula no llega a las elecciones como favorito, confía en poder protagonizar una remontada espectacular. Ya lo ha hecho antes. Tras pasar 580 días en prisión entre 2018 y 2019 por una condena por corrupción que posteriormente fue anulada, derrotó por un estrecho margen a Jair Bolsonaro en 2022. "Mientras yo viva, la extrema derecha no volverá al poder en este país", ha afirmado durante la campaña electoral. Lula y sus aliados siguen luchando contra lo que consideran una injerencia internacional destinada a impedirle un cuarto mandato. Su campaña acusó al gigante tecnológico estadounidense Meta, propietario de Instagram, WhatsApp y Facebook, de manipular las redes sociales días antes de las elecciones. Meta achacó el problema a fallos técnicos globales y negó cualquier sesgo político. Lula ha presentado a su oponente como un representante de un movimiento de derecha más amplio, compartiendo imágenes que lo vinculan con Trump, el presidente argentino Javier Milei y el primer ministro israelí Benjamin Netanyahu. Ante el triunfo arrollador de los partidos de derecha en las recientes elecciones en toda América Latina, Lula y sus aliados ven la segunda vuelta del domingo como una oportunidad para frenar el giro conservador de la región. "Lula es un símbolo de la lucha contra el imperialismo de Trump (...) de la liberación de América Latina y del mundo", afirmó Paulo Saboia, un técnico informático jubilado de 67 años, en un mitin de Lula en São Paulo.

item.title: Michigan Republican candidate and UAW, in rare alignment, blast GM
item.description: Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers and the United Auto Workers union found rare common ground on Tuesday, separately accusing General Motors of putting shareholders ahead of workers after the automaker unveiled a new $20 billion stock buyback plan.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers and the United Auto Workers union found rare common ground on Tuesday, separately accusing General Motors (GM.N) of putting shareholders ahead of workers after the automaker unveiled a new [USN:L6N4660PI TEXT:"$20 billion stock buyback"] plan. Rogers, a former US House member, accused GM of wrongly investing in electric vehicles. "GM lost billions investing in EVs nobody wanted. For two years, GM could have focused on reinvesting in Michigan workers and manufacturing vehicles consumers actually want to buy. Instead, they chose to put profits over people, and Michigan autoworkers will pay the price," Rogers said in a statement. Rogers is competing against Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in a [USN:L6N45U0XV TEXT:"closely watched Senate race"] and hopes to flip the seat to Republican control. Republicans have increasingly courted autoworkers and other blue-collar voters in Michigan, whose economy remains closely tied to the auto industry. Polls through mid-October generally show El-Sayed ahead in the November 3 election by a few points, though several surveys have fallen within the margin of error. The United Auto Workers, which has endorsed El-Sayed, also condemned the buyback, calling it "outrageous" when 80% of GM autoworkers do not have pensions or retiree healthcare benefits and saying the automaker was "choosing Wall Street profits over blue-collar America." Rogers did not elaborate on how GM's electric vehicle investments contributed to the buyback decision. The company has bought back about $29.5 billion in stock since 2023, and CEO Mary Barra said GM viewed its shares as undervalued. Asked to comment on the criticism, GM said its "first priority is investing in our business and our employees. Since 2020, we’ve reinvested more than $100 billion to fund our growth, including in our products, our factories, and our people." The criticism was unusual for Rogers, who has generally focused on denouncing government policies promoting electric vehicles rather than on automakers themselves. El-Sayed did not immediately respond to a request for comment. UAW President Shawn Fain said stock buybacks "are a form of legalized mass looting, sending billions of dollars generated by the working class directly to Wall Street investors who've never seen the inside of a factory." GM has scaled back electric vehicle production and investment plans amid softer EV demand and policy changes under President Donald Trump. The automaker has recorded $11.2 billion in EV-related charges since last year. Rogers has frequently criticized policies aimed at accelerating electric vehicle adoption and appeared with Trump at a campaign-style event at a GM facility in Michigan in July. The candidate and president argued such policies threaten US manufacturing jobs.

item.title: 欧州市場サマリー（20日）
item.description:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞
続落して取引を終えた。銀行株や資源関連株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は小幅に続落。中型株で構成す...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（20日） 4:18 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

続落して取引を終えた。銀行株や資源関連株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は小幅に続落。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．０６％安だった。

英労働市場統計によると、賃金上昇ペースはわずかに加速し、雇用に回復の兆しが見られた。ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、市場ではイングランド銀行（英中央銀行）が１１月に０．２５％ポイントの利上げを決めることがほぼ確実視されている。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種銀行株指数は０．８４％安。金融大手ＨＳＢＣ、ナットウエスト、ロイズは０．９─１．１％下落した。

資源株指数は１．５９％下落。石油大手のＢＰは１．７％、シェルは０．８％それぞれ下落した。

一方、公益事業株指数は１．５２％高。電力・ガス供給のナショナル・グリッドは１．８％上昇した。住宅建設株指数は３．２９％高。

ＪＰモルガンが目標株価を引き上げたオンラインスーパー大手オカドは１０．０％上昇した。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

続落して取引を終えた。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連投資への懸念などから、工業株の売り注文が優勢だった。フランスのＣＡＣ４０指数は０．３８％安と続落。経済の停滞や財政悪化といった課題を抱えるフランスで、激しい抗議デモが発生。約半年後に大統領選を控えることもあり、投資家の警戒感が強まっている。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種工業株指数は１．４３％安。データセンター関連を顧客とするスイス重電大手ＡＢＢは５．０％安。機関投資家から資金調達を実施した配電・制御機器大手シュナイダー・エレクトリックは３．３％下落。

一方、フランスのクラウド事業者のＯＶＨクラウドは１８．０％高。財務指標が改善し、買われた。直近の四半期決算が増収だった電子機器メーカーのコメット・ホールディングは４．７％上昇した。

ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、市場では、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が今月の理事会で金利を据え置いた後、１２月会合で利上げを決めることが有力視されている。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

フランス国債利回りが２４年ぶりの高水準近辺で推移した。抗議デモの拡大懸念を背景に前日は約1カ月ぶりの大幅上昇を記録し、この日も荒い値動きが続いた。終盤には小幅低下した。

フランス１０年国債（ＯＡＴ）利回りは終盤に３ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下の４．８８％。一時４．９８７７％まで上昇し、２００２年７月以来の高水準となった１０月初旬の４．９９３７％に迫った。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は約２．５ｂｐ拡大し、１５０ｂｐとなった。この利回り格差は１０月初旬に１５８．６７ｂｐと、２０１１年１１月以来の水準に拡大していた。

ゴールドマン・サックスのストラテジストらは「直接的な経済への影響は当面限定的にとどまるとみているが、混乱がさらに広がる可能性は、金融環境の引き締まり、政治的不確実性の高まり、緊縮財政によって既に弱まっている経済に、新たな逆風をもたらす」と指摘した。

一方、ユーロ圏の指標となるドイツ国債の利回りは低下したものの、最近のレンジ内にとどまった。エネルギー価格の上昇圧力が根強く、投資家は欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）の追加利上げ観測を後退させていない。

ドイツ１０年国債利回りは７ｂｐ低下の３．３８５％。

政策金利見通しに敏感なドイツ２年国債利回りは５ｂｐ低下し、３．０４５％となった。

独伊１０年債利回り格差は１．５７ｂｐ縮小し、１０９．５ｂｐとなった。

item.title: トランプ氏、ウクライナに和平合意促す 「ロシア戦場で優位」
item.description: [ワシントン ２０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ワシントン　２０日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２０日、ロシアとの戦争終結に向け、ウクライナに和平合意に応じるよう求めた。

トランプ氏はホワイトハウスの大統領執務室で記者団に対し、「ウクライナはこの戦争を終わらせたいと望まなければならない」と述べた。また、「ウクライナがこの戦争を終わらせるときが来た」とし、ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領が合意に応じることを望んでいると語った。

その上で、ロシアは戦場で優位に立っているとの認識を表明。「ロシアは巨大な機械のようなもので、ただ前進し続けており、実際にそうしてきた」とし、「ロシアは広大な領土を占領した」と述べた。

ゼレンスキー大統領はこの日、ノルウェーの首都オスロで米国のウィットコフ和平交渉担当特使と会談。会談後の記者会見で、ロシアによる弾道ミサイル攻撃に関する情報共有や早期警戒の提供を米国が再開したことに謝意を示した。

ノルウェーのストーレ首相によると、ウィットコフ氏は２１日にロシア第２の都市サンクトペテルブルクを訪問し、ロシア首脳部と会談する。

item.title: French education budget rises in cash terms, but key sectors lose millions in purchasing power
item.description: France’s 2027 budget increases overall education spending but secondary schools, universities and student programmes will lose hundreds of millions of euros when inflation is factored in, a Reuters analysis finds, despite a government post missing that context.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: France’s 2027 budget increases overall education spending but secondary schools, universities and student programmes will lose hundreds of millions of euros when inflation is factored in, a Reuters analysis finds, despite a government post missing that context. "Soyons Clair" ("Let's Be Clear"), the French government's newly launched social media fact-checking account, said on X in early October that opposition lawmaker Éric Coquerel was incorrect in claiming the proposed 2027 budget cut €840 million ($942 million) from schools and higher education budgets compared with this year. “A €840 million cut to education and higher education? That’s false,” the account said on October 5, as [USN:L8N45S08G TEXT:"violent protests"] by high school students swept across the country. The day before, Coquerel had referenced French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu in an X post that said, in part, “Education and higher education budgets are declining! If we take 2.1% inflation into account, which makes sense, the secondary plus university budget … is down -840 M€.” The government’s fact-checking account disputed Coquerel’s post by citing the budget’s education spending increases, including an extra €1.1 billion for schools and an additional €423 million for higher education and research. The Education Ministry says its total budget for 2027 will reach €89.1 billion, representing an increase of €1.2 billion, or 1.9% over 2026 spending. However, the figures cited by the government refer to an increase in the ministry’s overall spend, whereas Coquerel focused just on secondary schools, student programmes and higher education, and used the government’s own latest 2.1% annual inflation measurement to calculate an effective cut in those categories for 2027. Coquerel referred to three specific segments in the education budget: public secondary education, university education and research, and student life, while figures cited by the government’s fact-checking account refer to sectors that Coquerel did not mention, including primary schools. The government's broader Education Ministry budget of €89.1 billion includes primary education, private schools under contract, agricultural education, central administration and other research programmes. Its largest headline figure – for a €1.2 billion overall increase - also includes state pension contributions. Public secondary education, covering middle and high schools, is allocated €40.284 billion in 2027, up from €40.002 billion in 2026 - an increase of roughly €282 million, the draft 2027 budget shows. But adjusting for 2.1% inflation, the programme is about €558 million below the amount needed to maintain its 2026 purchasing power. Likewise, the university education and research programme rises from €15.724 billion in 2026 to €15.786 billion in 2027 but remains about €268 million below its inflation-adjusted 2026 level. The student-life programme, which includes grants and support services, rises to €3.331 billion, from €3.275 billion, but is about €13 million short after inflation. Together, the nominal budget for those three categories increases by €399 million, or about 0.68%. But the inflation-adjusted shortfalls total roughly €839 million, which is a close match to Coquerel's €840 million figure, Reuters found. If the government’s 2027 official inflation forecast of 1.8% is used, instead of the July 2026 estimate of 2.1%, the inflation-adjusted decrease for those three categories in the 2027 budget is €662 million, Reuters calculated. A final vote on the draft budget legislation is expected in mid-November. VERDICT Missing context. French education spending rises in 2027, including a nominal increase of €399 million in three categories cited in Éric Coquerel’s social media post, however when the same budget figures are adjusted for inflation, spending in those categories falls by up to €839 million.

item.title: At least 17 data center campuses proposed on US public lands, group says
item.description: At least 35 data center-related applications covering more than 24,000 acres of US federal land are pending or active across six Western states, according to an analysis by conservation group Center for Western Priorities.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least 35 data center-related applications covering more than 24,000 acres of US federal land are pending or active across six Western states, according to an analysis by conservation group Center for Western Priorities. US Bureau of Land Management records show at least 17 proposed data center campuses and 13 related infrastructure projects, including transmission lines, pipelines, telecommunications facilities and access roads across Arizona, Idaho, Nevada, Oregon, Utah and Wyoming, according to the study. A map of the planned projects includes several applications for infrastructure tied to a Prometheus Hyperscale facility in Wyoming and a range of projects by developer Copia Power in Arizona, Nevada and Idaho, among others. The figures underscore industry interest in developing AI infrastructure on federal land as the Trump administration seeks to open public lands to a wider range of industrial uses, including energy, mining and technology projects. US President Donald Trump's administration has strongly [USN:L8N3ZL04J TEXT:"backed"] data center expansion as a national priority, but the public is increasingly [USN:L1N3WX0S4 TEXT:"opposed"] to such projects, citing concerns about electricity demand, water consumption, wildlife impacts and public access to federal lands. BLM officials were not immediately available for comment.

item.title: Texas federal judge with suspected mental condition urged to reengage with inquiry
item.description: A committee of judicial investigators on Tuesday implored a federal judge in Texas suspected of suffering from a mental condition to cooperate and explain why she emailed confidential and sealed court documents to about 140 judges, lawyers and members of the press over the weekend.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A committee of judicial investigators on Tuesday implored a federal judge in Texas [USN:L1N4650ZG TEXT:"suspected"] of suffering from a mental condition to cooperate and explain why she emailed confidential and sealed court documents to about 140 judges, lawyers and members of the press over the weekend. The three-judge committee, in an order released by the 5th Circuit Judicial Council, said that US District Judge Ada Brown of Dallas sent an email after 1 a.m. on Saturday rejecting its request that she sit for an interview on October 30 as part of a judicial misconduct inquiry into her recent conduct. The committee sought the interview after earlier determining Brown had "abandoned her post as a federal judge" and likely suffers from a mental condition interfering with her ability to perform the responsibilities of her office, citing "bizarre emails" and "racial insults" it said she made. Based on those allegations, the committee on September 21 took the rare step of ordering Brown to sit for a psychiatric exam within 30 days, and the judicial council on September 29 ordered her cases to be reassigned temporarily and that no further cases be assigned to her, according to documents released on Monday. The committee in Tuesday's order said Brown on Saturday declined to participate in the proceedings, claiming it would "necessarily compromise a parallel investigation outside the jurisdiction of the Fifth Circuit." The panel said it had no knowledge of such an outside probe. Brown then sent documents from the confidential judicial misconduct proceedings against her as well as records from two seemingly unrelated attorney-discipline matters to numerous judges, lawyers and members of the media, the committee said. "The Committee urges Judge Brown to reconsider her decision not to participate," Tuesday's order said. "Failure to cooperate and comply with this Committee’s orders, without good cause shown, may result in the Committee expanding the scope of the investigation." Brown, who was appointed to the US District Court for the Northern District of Texas by President Donald Trump during his first term, did not respond to requests for comment. The committee in Tuesday's order directed Brown to provide by October 27 information on who is conducting the purported parallel investigation she referred to and to explain why she leaked confidential and sealed records. Should Brown continue to refuse to cooperate, the panel warned that it would be forced to complete its investigation and submit recommendations for potential action by the judicial council without the benefit of Brown's response, and would also examine whether her refusal to cooperate constituted misconduct. The committee's members include Chief US Circuit Judge Jennifer Walker Elrod, who initiated one of two judicial misconduct complaints against Brown; US Circuit Judge James Graves; and Chief US District Judge Alia Moses of the Western District of Texas. Read more: [USN:L1N4650ZG TEXT:"Texas federal judge suspended from hearing cases over mental health concerns"]

item.title: Three issues defining the 2026 US midterm elections
item.description: President Donald Trump’s record-low popularity, voter frustration over the cost of living and a fierce immigration fight are shaping the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine whether Republicans keep control of Congress or Democrats gain the power to challenge his administration.
item.dc:creator: Nolan Mccaskill
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump’s record-low popularity, voter frustration over the cost of living and a fierce immigration fight are shaping the November 3 midterm elections , which will determine whether Republicans keep control of Congress or Democrats gain the power to challenge his administration. Republicans hold narrow majorities in the House of Representatives and Senate. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control of each chamber. The outcome will hinge on a relatively small number of competitive races, but the campaigns are being shaped nationally by Trump himself and voter concerns over affordability and immigration. Here is a look at the three issues defining the election: DONALD TRUMP The president has put himself front and center in the closing stretch of the campaign cycle despite his record-low popularity, with upcoming rallies in Florida, Iowa, Michigan and Texas. Trump's approval rating has fallen to an all-time low 31%, according to a [USN:L6N465159 TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos poll"]. Yet he has repeatedly urged voters to pretend he's on the ballot, an effort that could motivate Democrats and independents to rally against his party despite the message being aimed at increasing turnout among Trump's base. Democrats have said Trump has broken his campaign promises to lower costs and end wars. They have vowed to tackle an affordability agenda to reduce Americans' cost of living and hold the administration accountable for alleged corruption if voters give them control of either chamber. AFFORDABILITY Voters have consistently ranked the cost of living as the top issue this election cycle. Half of registered voters surveyed in a recent Reuters/Ipsos poll cited the cost of living as the most important factor in how they will vote. In the same poll, voters highlighted healthcare, gasoline, food and housing as the top household bills lawmakers should focus on. Republicans' top legislative achievement was a tax cut extension that slashed roughly $1 trillion in spending for Medicaid, the government health insurance program for low-income Americans, and other health programs. Democrats last year forced a government shutdown over a failed effort to extend expiring health subsidies that benefited 24 million Americans. Gas prices have spiked since the US and Israel launched military strikes on Iran in February. The national average price of gas is $4.28 — $1.20 higher than it was a year ago, according to AAA. The average cost of diesel is $6.32 — a $2.70 increase from a year earlier. Grocery costs are up 1.8% over the past year, according to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics data on consumer prices. Federal Housing Finance Agency data show home prices rose 2.1% over the past year. Congress passed a bipartisan housing bill earlier this year. It became law without Trump's signature. IMMIGRATION Preliminary data from the Department of Homeland Security showed a 95% drop in migrants apprehended at the southwest border compared to former President Joe Biden's administration. The agency said there have been no Border Patrol releases the entire fiscal year for the first time ever. But fatal encounters with federal immigration agents have occurred in Maine, Minnesota and Texas. The backlash to the death of two US citizens in Minnesota pulled many Democrats in competitive primaries to the left this year, with some candidates calling for the impeachment of then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and others saying Immigration and Customs Enforcement should be abolished. Democrats and Republicans sparred over immigration funding this year in a stalemate that forced Republicans to unilaterally pass a $70 billion bill to fund ICE and the Border Patrol for the remainder of Trump's presidency. Republicans counter Democrats' criticism by saying Democrats support open borders. Federal immigration officials also [USN:L1N45Y0CB TEXT:"raided the Washington home"] of Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota this month, drawing widespread condemnation from Democrats. A person familiar with the case against Omar told Reuters one potential aim of the investigation could be to [USN:L6N46118Z TEXT:"strip her of US citizenship and deport her"]. OTHER ISSUES Artificial intelligence and data centers, cryptocurrency, abortion and Israel could also influence voters in individual races. In Ohio's Senate race, for example, Democratic nominee Sherrod Brown has labeled Republican Senator Jon Husted the face of data centers, and the crypto super PAC Defend American Jobs has spent more than $46 million to reelect Husted over Brown, a former US senator who chaired the chamber's Banking Committee. In Maine's Senate race, Democratic nominee Troy Jackson is hoping voters don't forget that Republican Senator Susan Collins helped confirm Brett Kavanaugh to the Supreme Court, which later overturned the federal right to abortion. Collins is on the election ballot for the first time since the high court made abortion a state issue rather than a federal right. In Michigan, Republican nominee Mike Rogers has indicated he would accept help from a pro-Israel super PAC that spent more than $30 million backing Democratic US Representative Haley Stevens in her unsuccessful primary against Abdul El-Sayed, who now faces Rogers in the general election. The group has already spent more than $280,000 on mailers against El-Sayed. Earlier this week, Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection.

item.title: Trump diz que Ucrânia precisa querer chegar a um acordo para pôr fim à guerra
item.description: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, pediu nesta terça-feira que a Ucrânia chegue a um acordo para encerrar a guerra com a Rússia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, pediu nesta terça-feira que a Ucrânia chegue a um acordo para encerrar a guerra com a Rússia. “A Ucrânia precisa querer resolver essa guerra”, disse Trump a jornalistas no Salão Oval. O enviado de Trump, Steve Witkoff, esteve nesta terça-feira em Oslo, na Noruega, para conversar com o presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, na busca de uma solução para a invasão russa da Ucrânia, que já dura quatro anos. Trump sugeriu que Moscou tem a vantagem na disputa porque "a Rússia é uma grande máquina -- eles simplesmente continuam avançando, e foi isso que fizeram". "Eles tomaram uma porção muito grande de terra."

item.title: Trump says he asked Putin to release American Stephen Hubbard
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he has raised with Russian President Vladimir Putin the issue of Stephen Hubbard, a retired American school teacher held by Moscow, and hinted that a development in the case could happen soon.
item.dc:creator: Steve Holland, Trevor Hunnicutt
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he has raised with Russian President Vladimir Putin the issue of Stephen Hubbard, a retired American school teacher held by Moscow, and hinted that a development in the case could happen soon. Trump made the comment to reporters in the Oval Office as US envoy Steve Witkoff prepared to go to Moscow for more talks about Ukraine after meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy in Oslo on Tuesday. In his remarks, Trump piled more pressure on Zelenskiy to make a deal with Russia to end Moscow's four-year war in Ukraine. "Ukraine has to want to settle this war," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. Trump suggested Moscow had the upper hand in the fight because "Russia is a big machine - they just keep grinding forward, and that's what they've done. They've taken a very large piece of land." Trump, asked about the case of Hubbard, said he had been talking to Putin about the American, who has been declared wrongfully detained by the State Department. "Just stick with me," said Trump. "I don't want to talk about it, but everybody has been after Hubbard for a long time, long before I got here. And just remember that question for a couple of days from now, okay? Because I do things that nobody else can do. " "Watch what happens. We have been focused on Hubbard," he said. Hubbard, 74, is serving a nearly seven-year sentence in a Russian penal colony on mercenary charges.

item.title: For Lula, Brazil's sovereignty is at stake in final election
item.description: When Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva addressed the United Nations General Assembly last month, he used one of the world’s biggest diplomatic stages to deliver a message that has come to define what is likely the final presidential campaign of his decades-long career.
item.dc:creator: Brendan O'Boyle, Lisandra Paraguassu
item.content:encoded: When Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva addressed the United Nations General Assembly last month, he used one of the world’s biggest diplomatic stages to deliver a message that has come to define what is likely the final presidential campaign of his decades-long career. "Brazil does not fit into anyone's backyard," he said, in a veiled dig at US President Donald Trump's administration, which he believes is challenging Brazil's sovereignty. Lula has portrayed Brazil's election as part of a wider battle against undemocratic forces, warning of "[USN:S0N44O041 TEXT:"foreign interference"]" in a race that concludes on Sunday in a heated runoff against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. In the candidates' first debate days before the vote, Lula accused the Bolsonaro family, headed by former President Jair Bolsonaro, of being "subordinate to American interests," pointing to May meetings between the Bolsonaros and Trump earlier this year before Trump imposed new tariffs on Brazilian products. In July, Lula said the new tariffs were the result of a "plot" with the Bolsonaros "driven by electoral objectives." Last year, the senator's brother Eduardo Bolsonaro, who lives in the US, described Trump's tariffs on Brazilian beef, coffee, fish, footwear and other goods as "bitter medicine" aimed at curbing what he called an out-of-check legal offensive against his father. “The pressure they applied to get the United States to put tariffs on Brazil, and their appeal for Brazil to suffer some harm," Lula said at the debate. "The brother is over there inciting a coup against Brazil." The family denied the accusations. The State Department has also denied previous accusations of election interference. HARD PATH TO VICTORY The election's [USN:L6N45N1A0 TEXT:"first round"] showed the limits to Lula's message. Over 47% of voters backed Bolsonaro, an outspoken Trump ally, nearly 2 percentage points ahead of Lula. Lula enters the final days trailing slightly in the polls to Bolsonaro, whose father is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a failed coup against Lula's electoral win in 2022. Although Lula enters the election as the underdog, he is confident he can stage a dramatic comeback. He has done so before. After spending 580 days in prison in 2018 and 2019 on a corruption conviction that was later overturned, he narrowly defeated Jair Bolsonaro in 2022. "As long as I am alive, the far right will not return to power in this country," he has said on the campaign trail. ALLIES VIEW HIM AS BULWARK AGAINST US POWER Lula and his allies continue to fight what they see as international interference to keep him from a fourth term. His campaign accused US tech giant Meta, which owns Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook, of manipulating social media days before the vote. Meta blamed global technical glitches and denied political bias. Lula has portrayed his opponent as a stand-in for a broader right-wing movement, sharing images linking him to Trump, Argentina’s President Javier Milei and Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. With right-wing parties sweeping recent elections across Latin America, Lula and his allies see Sunday’s runoff as a chance to stem [USN:L4N42T01C TEXT:"the region's conservative drift"]. “Lula is a symbol of the fight against Trump’s imperialism ... of the liberation of Latin America and the world,” Paulo Saboia, a 67-year-old retired IT technician, said at a Lula rally in Sao Paulo.

item.title: France backs UNESCO drive to involve more young people in political decisions
item.description: A UNESCO drive to get more young people into decision-making bodies, including those on how to prevent wars, won the backing of France's foreign minister on Tuesday, as the country faces a wave of student protests, many of which have turned violent.
item.dc:creator: John Irish
item.content:encoded: A UNESCO drive to get more young people into decision-making bodies, including those on how to prevent wars, won the backing of France's foreign minister on Tuesday, as the country faces a wave of student [USN:L6N4660DJ TEXT:"protests"], many of which have turned violent. The appeal, formally adopted by the UN's cultural and education agency after being drafted by 145 young representatives from 135 countries, calls for youth representation in decision-making bodies, conflict prevention and mediation mechanisms. The initiative comes at a time where student-led protests in recent weeks have highlighted frustration among some young people over their perceived lack of influence on political decisions. "Young people's voices matter," Jean-Noel Barrot said on X following UNESCO's backing of the appeal. The UNESCO proposal also urged governments to establish an international framework to govern artificial intelligence, which the signatories describe as a new threat to peace, and to create public mechanisms to monitor implementation of their recommendations. High school students are due to join a new round of national protests on Saturday vowing to bring the government to account over what they call a dysfunctional system, worsened by spending cuts spurred by France's budget crunch, with student bodies demanding to be heard. "Peace among nations, like civic peace, rests on the ability of enlightened women and men to settle their differences respectfully, recognising that they share a common future," added Barrot.

item.title: EQT in advanced talks to buy testing firm Qiagen, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: European molecular testing company Qiagen is in advanced talks to be acquired by Swedish buyout firm EQT , Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: European molecular testing company Qiagen (QIA.DE) is in advanced talks to be acquired by Swedish buyout firm EQT (EQTAB.ST) , Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter. US-listed shares of Qiagen were up over 6% in afternoon trading. The company has a market capitalization of €8.57 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. Qiagen's board is meeting this week to decide on the potential deal, the report said, citing people familiar with the talks. There is no certainty the discussions will lead to a sale to EQT or another buyer, the report added. EQT has submitted a binding offer of more than $50 per share for Qiagen, while US private equity firm KKR has also made a bid, Bloomberg News reported. The reported talks come after Qiagen said [USN:L4N3YL1R1 TEXT:"in January"] it was evaluating strategic options amid renewed takeover interest. Interest in the diagnostics company continued through the year, with buyout firms including EQT, Advent and KKR linked to a potential acquisition in July. Qiagen develops molecular testing and sample-preparation technologies used by research and clinical laboratories. KKR declined to comment, while EQT did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment. Qiagen said it does not comment on "market rumors or speculation." ($1 = 0.9259 euros)

item.title: Ataque israelense mata quatro pessoas em Gaza, segundo equipes médicas
item.description: Ataques aéreos e disparos israelenses mataram pelo menos quatro palestinos, incluindo um casal e um jovem de 17 anos, em incidentes separados na Faixa de Gaza na terça-feira, informaram autoridades de saúde.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ataques aéreos e disparos israelenses mataram pelo menos quatro palestinos, incluindo um casal e um jovem de 17 anos, em incidentes separados na Faixa de Gaza na terça-feira, informaram autoridades de saúde. Médicos informaram que um ataque aéreo israelense matou Akram Yassin e sua esposa, Dina Abu Baker, em um apartamento na Cidade de Gaza. O Exército israelense afirmou em um comunicado, horas depois, que Yassin era uma autoridade de alto escalão do aparato de segurança geral do Hamas na Faixa de Gaza. O comunicado indicou que o aparato tinha a função de proteger altos dirigentes do Hamas. Em Khan Younis, no sul, equipes médicas informaram que um adolescente de 17 anos foi morto por tiros israelenses perto do bairro de Qizan Al-Najar, enquanto outro foi morto por tiros israelenses no subúrbio de Zeitoun, a leste da cidade de Gaza, elevando o número de mortos nesta terça-feira para pelo menos quatro. As forças armadas israelenses não se pronunciaram imediatamente sobre nenhum desses dois incidentes. Palestinos inspecionavam os estragos causados pelo ataque ao apartamento na Cidade de Gaza antes de se reunirem para o funeral do casal. “Supostamente, estamos em um período de cessar-fogo, mas, honestamente, não estamos vendo nenhum cessar-fogo nem nada parecido. A guerra ainda continua, os assassinatos seguem ocorrendo e os bombardeios não pararam”, disse Mahmoud Yassin, cujo irmão foi morto. Israel, que acusa o grupo militante Hamas de estar se rearmando e lançando ataques em violação ao cessar-fogo, intensificou os ataques contra o grupo nas últimas semanas. O Hamas negou estar tentando realizar ataques ou reconstruir seu arsenal e acusa Israel de minar o acordo de paz de Gaza. Mediado pelos EUA há um ano, o cessar-fogo prevê uma futura reconstrução do território. Mas pouco progresso foi feito na implementação de um acordo para pôr fim ao conflito, que inclui cláusulas para que o Hamas se desarme e Israel retire suas tropas. Autoridades de saúde de Gaza afirmaram que pelo menos 1.500 palestinos foram mortos por disparos israelenses desde o cessar-fogo. Israel afirma que quatro de seus soldados foram mortos por militantes em Gaza no mesmo período.

item.title: Meloni aprova leis antitumulto mais rigorosas após episódios de violência em Milão
item.description: A Itália aprovou, nesta terça-feira, um pacote de medidas de segurança, incluindo um novo crime de participação violenta em manifestações, penas mais severas para os manifestantes violentos e responsabilidade financeira para os pais cujos filhos participem de atos de vandalismo e saques.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Fonte, Emilio Parodi, Anna Uras
item.content:encoded: A Itália aprovou, nesta terça-feira, um pacote de medidas de segurança, incluindo um novo crime de participação violenta em manifestações, penas mais severas para os manifestantes violentos e responsabilidade financeira para os pais cujos filhos participem de atos de vandalismo e saques. A medida foi tomada após distúrbios terem assolado cidades do norte da Itália no fim de semana, incluindo a capital financeira, Milão, onde grupos compostos principalmente por jovens causaram tumultos, quebrando vitrines, saqueando lojas e atacando a polícia. “Não há nada de revolucionário em vandalizar e roubar. Vandalismo e roubo não são protesto, são criminalidade”, afirmou a primeira-ministra, Giorgia Meloni, nas redes sociais, ao divulgar o decreto. Como parte do pacote, que entra em vigor imediatamente, qualquer pessoa que participar de um grupo de pelo menos cinco pessoas e colocar em risco a segurança pública durante protestos pode pegar até cinco anos de prisão e uma multa máxima de 20.000 euros. As penalidades aumentam se os rostos estiverem ocultos ou se houver feridos. As autoridades têm o poder de ordenar a indenização imediata por quaisquer danos causados e, no caso de menores, seus pais serão responsabilizados. A polícia terá permissão para deter jovens com idades entre 14 e 17 anos, mesmo que não tenham cometido um crime, desde que haja evidências de que representam um perigo, ampliando os poderes que antes se aplicavam apenas a adultos. Embora as autoridades temam novos distúrbios nas manifestações planejadas para sábado, o governo afirmou que mobilizará 500 soldados do Exército para atuarem ao lado da polícia em Milão até o final de 2026. Os militares ajudarão a reforçar a segurança em locais-chave, intensificarão a vigilância em áreas sensíveis e aprimorarão o monitoramento em toda a região, informou o Ministério da Defesa em comunicado. A CAMPANHA DE SEGURANÇA DE MELONI Os distúrbios no norte da Itália ecoaram os tumultos na vizinha França, onde centenas de milhares de pessoas saíram às ruas no sábado, em alguns dos episódios de agitação mais violentos do país nos últimos anos. Meloni vem aprovando uma série contínua de medidas de repressão à insegurança desde que assumiu o cargo em 2022, medidas que, segundo críticos, pouco contribuem para resolver as causas subjacentes da criminalidade e da desordem. A população carcerária da Itália aumentou mais de 17% em quatro anos, ou quase 10 mil pessoas, segundo dados do governo. O governo de Meloni também enfrenta pressão crescente de uma onda separada de protestos no sul da Itália, onde caminhoneiros indignados com a alta vertiginosa dos preços do diesel e o aumento do custo de vida montaram bloqueios nas estradas que estão prejudicando as cadeias de abastecimento. Algumas fábricas de massas tiveram que interromper a produção, e grupos agrícolas alertaram que frutas e verduras podem acabar apodrecendo. O governo prometeu novos auxílios aos transportadores rodoviários após negociações com representantes do setor. Manifestantes tanto no norte quanto no sul afirmam que o aumento dos preços está levando as famílias à pobreza — uma preocupação para Meloni diante das eleições nacionais previstas para 2027. “Sabemos o que significa procurar emprego, receber um salário insuficiente e não ver perspectivas para o futuro... mas as dificuldades nunca devem ser usadas como desculpa para a violência”, disse a primeira-ministra nesta terça-feira.

item.title: iFood compra empresa de benefícios Caju e dobra presença no setor de vales-alimentação
item.description: O iFood, aplicativo de entrega de comida controlado pela investidora holandesa Prosus , anunciou nesta terça-feira a compra da Caju, empresa de benefícios corporativos e atuante no mercado de vales-refeição e vales-alimentação.
item.dc:creator: Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
item.content:encoded: O iFood, aplicativo de entrega de comida controlado pela investidora holandesa Prosus (PRX.AS) , anunciou nesta terça-feira a compra da Caju, empresa de benefícios corporativos e atuante no mercado de vales-refeição e vales-alimentação. Com a compra da Caju o iFood busca crescer além do seu serviço principal de entregas, mirando também segmento de benefícios a funcionários. O iFood domina o setor de delivery no Brasil, que hoje vive um acirramento da concorrência , após a chegada da Keeta, unidade do gigante chinês de tecnologia Meituan (3690.HK) . Se aprovada pelos órgãos reguladores locais, a aquisição dobrará a presença do iFood no setor de benefícios corporativos, disseram as empresas em um comunicado conjunto. Os termos financeiros do negócio, realizado por meio do iFood Benefícios, braço de benefícios corporativos do iFood, não foram divulgados. No entanto, a aquisição faz parte do plano mais amplo do iFood de investir R$24 bilhões até março de 2027, informou o comunicado. O crescente mercado de vales-refeição e vales-alimentação do Brasil movimenta cerca de R$150 bilhões por ano entre mais de 20 milhões de consumidores, de acordo com Arthur Freitas, CEO do iFood Benefícios. O iFood Benefícios e a Caju processam, cada um, cerca de R$1,3 bilhão em transações mensais, disse Freitas à Reuters em entrevista. Juntas, as duas empresas atenderão aproximadamente 135 mil clientes corporativos e 3 milhões de usuários ativos, acrescentou. O negócio ainda depende da aprovação do Banco Central e do Cade, com conclusão prevista para o próximo ano, segundo Eduardo Del Giglio, cofundador e CEO da Caju.

item.title: Feared extinct, Bangka slow loris primate rediscovered in Indonesia
item.description: The Bangka slow loris is one of Earth's most exotic primates, a slow-moving tree dweller that happens to be venomous. It was listed as critically endangered and possibly extinct, last scientifically documented in the 1930s, but now has been rediscovered on the tropical Indonesian island of Bangka.
item.dc:creator: Will Dunham
item.content:encoded: The Bangka slow loris is one of Earth's most exotic primates, a slow-moving tree dweller that happens to be venomous. It was listed as critically endangered and possibly extinct, last scientifically documented in the 1930s, but now has been rediscovered on the tropical Indonesian island of Bangka. Scientists revealed in a new study that an animal rescue organization came across more than 90 Bangka slow loris individuals in recent years on Bangka, located off the southeastern coast of Sumatra. Most were returned to the wild. "The Bangka slow loris is still alive," said Timon Glaw, a graduate student in nature conservation and biodiversity management at the Haus des Meeres Aqua Terra Zoo in Vienna, Austria, and one of the authors of the study published in the journal Spixiana . The rescued animals came from different parts of Bangka, showing the species has survived in several areas despite extensive habitat destruction and decades of scientific neglect, Glaw said. Its habitat has been diminished due to tin mining and land clearing for oil palm plantations, Glaw said. "What I find particularly astonishing is that such a charismatic and distinctive primate has received so little scientific attention for nearly a century. Its rediscovery also offers hope that other species feared to be extinct may still survive in places where scientists have not looked for decades. After all, Bangka is just about an hour flight from Jakarta, one of the largest cities in the world," Glaw said. The Bangka slow loris, whose scientific name is Nycticebus bancanus, is a relatively small, nocturnal primate, with reddish-brown fur, distinctive facial markings and large eyes. It moves slowly and deliberately in the trees, unlike other arboreal primates such as apes, monkeys and lemurs that can move quickly across branches. In the primate evolutionary lineage, the Bangka slow loris is more closely related to the lemurs of Madagascar and the galagos of Africa than to monkeys or apes — or people. "The last historical scientific records from Bangka discussed in our study date back to the early 1930s, more precisely to the period between 1930 and 1932. For decades, there was no reliable information on whether the species survived on the island," Glaw said. In 2020, the International Union for Conservation of Nature, the organization that monitors the status of species, deemed the Bangka slow loris critically endangered and possibly extinct. The species also was listed as one of the "lost primates" by the conservation group Re:wild. A VENOMOUS BITE Like the world's other slow loris species, it is venomous — a rare trait among mammals. Slow lorises produce a secretion from specialized glands near their elbows, which they mix with saliva by raising their arms when threatened and then licking the glands before delivering the venom through a bite. "The venom can cause severe allergic reactions in humans, potentially even life-threatening ones. Research on other slow loris species suggests that the venom is used primarily in conflicts with other lorises, although it may also serve defensive functions against predators and parasites," Glaw said. Its diet is not well understood, but it likely feeds on insects, tree gums, nectar and other plant parts like other slow loris species, Glaw said. It possesses a toothcomb formed by forward-projecting lower teeth, used mainly for grooming, gouging of tree bark for gum and delivering the venom during bites. It also has a specialized second tongue beneath the main tongue that helps clean the toothcomb. Between 2015 and 2025, the Indonesian conservation organization Alobi Wildlife Rescue Center documented more than 90 Bangka slow lorises from different localities across the island, Glaw said. Many were rescued from houses, gardens, plantations or roads, while others suffered severe injuries, particularly from electrical wires, with a few dying despite treatment, Glaw said. Following their recovery, 86 of them were released into suitable natural habitats, Glaw said. "The most urgent priority is to protect the remaining natural forests on Bangka from further destruction, particularly through tin mining and the expansion of oil palm plantations. We also need systematic field surveys to determine where the species still survives and how large its populations are," Glaw said. "Every species is the result of millions of years of evolution and part of a complex ecological network, and losing the Bangka slow loris would mean losing something truly irreplaceable," Glaw said.

item.title: Nvidia emerges as the central bank of AI
item.description: The $5.3 trln firm has helped prop up buyers of its own chips, including under-pressure data-center operator CoreWeave. Boss Jensen Huang says that the so-called neocloud is strong enough to stand on its own. A freeze in credit markets could force his hand.
item.dc:creator: Pranav Kiran
item.content:encoded: Call it the Bank of Jensen. Chipmaker Nvidia’s (NVDA.O) outspoken CEO Jensen Huang has pledged massive support to keep the artificial intelligence economy humming. That includes a backstop for CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , whose shares are slumping as it burns cash to stuff data centers with Nvidia chips. Huang insists that the so-called neocloud is strong enough to stand alone. If lenders grow leery, though, the $5.3 trillion chipmaker’s role as a kind of central bank for the industry could be tested. Neoclouds borrow money to build server farms for blue-chip tech giants like Microsoft (MSFT.O) through to AI labs like Anthropic. Long-term contracts fetch about $10 million per megawatt of capacity and can give lenders confidence to fork over billions in debt. Yet truly juicy pricing, of perhaps $40 million per megawatt, goes to shorter-term deals. With interest rates rising and neocloud debt selling off, the risk is that cheaper deals no longer clear companies’ cost of capital while funding becomes too stringent to chase richer opportunities. Huang, like any good central banker, has been trying to ensure liquidity. Nvidia not only invested [USN:L4N3YR124 TEXT:"$2 billion"] in CoreWeave’s equity, but in September inked a $6.3 billion agreement to purchase any unsold capacity through 2032. That should help smooth a move away from long-term contracts. The company employs credit facilities that pair chip purchases with specific customer contracts against which they’re secured. Early versions matched the maturity of the facility with the length of the contract. A more recent iteration, however, raised five-year debt against three-year agreements, introducing renewal risk. Nvidia should be able to help defray that by being a customer of last resort. It’s important for Huang to keep this market humming: customers including neoclouds accounted for 45% of Nvidia’s $89 billion in data-center revenue last quarter, with so-called hyperscalers like Microsoft making up the rest, according to Visible Alpha data. Bank of America analysts [USN:L6N44N16H TEXT:"reckon"] that Nvidia’s backstop commitments across the AI ecosystem total $230 billion. The real nightmare scenario is that neoclouds can’t renew contracts, or that customers begin to default, destabilizing the guarantees on which lenders depend and freezing them out of credit markets. This is, to be clear, hypothetical. But it would threaten a massive source of demand for Nvidia. At that point, Huang’s backstops would be tested. The Federal Reserve was able to extend vast support to the economy when credit froze up during the 2008 crisis. But Nvidia is not actually a money-printing central bank: presumably, if its customers suffer, so too will its own cash flow. The company can only sustain the AI boom so far. Follow Pranav Kiran on Bluesky and X . “CoreWeave’s strength is improving every day,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told Bloomberg at an event on October 15 in Stockholm. “I’m optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually decreasing.” CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Anthropic's public benefit fund and how it compares with other big philanthropic efforts
item.description: Anthropic said it would commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund, as debate intensifies over how the growing wealth generated by artificial intelligence should be distributed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic said it would commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund, as debate intensifies over how the growing wealth generated by artificial intelligence should be distributed. The pledge comes amid a broader political debate over who should benefit from AI's gains, months after US Senator Bernie Sanders introduced a bill that would give the public a 50% stake in the largest US AI companies. Here is what is known about Anthropic's fund and how it compares with some other large philanthropic efforts set up by major corporations, their current or former leaders, or their families: ANTHROPIC PUBLIC BENEFIT FUND Anthropic [USN:L4N46403A TEXT:"said"] in a blog post on Sunday its Public Benefit Fund could support initiatives including nonprofit donations, direct distributions to specific populations and efforts to address AI's impact on the labor market. The Claude maker said its proposed fund would be established as a wholly owned limited liability company and would receive an additional 2% of Anthropic's shares, at the board's discretion, for every 50% increase in the company's value above a baseline that has yet to be disclosed. OPENAI FOUNDATION OpenAI completed a [USN:L4N3W91HS TEXT:"restructuring"] in October 2025 that left its nonprofit, renamed the OpenAI Foundation, with a 26% stake in the for-profit, worth about $130 billion at the time. The foundation also holds a warrant to receive additional equity if OpenAI Group's share price rises more than tenfold over 15 years. OpenAI said in a blog post at that time that the company's success will raise the value of the nonprofit's stake, which the nonprofit will use to fund its philanthropic work. The foundation said it will initially focus on a $25 billion commitment across two areas: health and curing diseases, and technical solutions to AI resilience. This builds on its $50 million commitment to support nonprofits and mission-focused organizations that OpenAI announced in July 2025. GATES FOUNDATION Founded in 2000 by Microsoft (MSFT.O) co-founder Bill Gates and his then-wife, Melinda French Gates, the Gates Foundation invested more than $102.3 billion during its first 25 years in global health and development, US education and economic mobility. In May 2025, Gates said the foundation would spend an additional $200 billion over the next two decades before winding down in December 2045. The foundation's work through 2045 will focus on three goals: ensuring that no mother or baby dies from a preventable cause, enabling the next generation to grow up without deadly infectious diseases, and helping hundreds of millions of people escape poverty. It plans a record $9 billion payout in 2026, with about 70% of its budget allocated to advancing those first two goals, which encompass its global health work. WARREN BUFFETT'S PLEDGE In 2006, the legendary investor Warren Buffett pledged to donate nearly all of his Berkshire stock to philanthropic foundations. Since then, he has donated over half of his shares, including more than $47 billion to the Gates Foundation and over $17 billion to four family charities. However, he [USN:L6N43G0T3 TEXT:"stopped"] donating to the Gates Foundation following revelations about interactions between Bill Gates and the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, ending a two-decade philanthropic partnership. Buffett said [USN:L2N3MW0D5 TEXT:"that he plans to donate"] 99.5% of his remaining wealth to a charitable trust overseen by his daughter and two sons when he dies. After his death, his children will have about 10 years to give away his remaining wealth and must decide unanimously which philanthropic purposes it should serve. ELON MUSK'S PLEDGE After Anthropic announced its public fund on Sunday, Elon Musk pledged to give one SpaceX share to "every kid in America." "Yes, giving shares, which are stakes in the future economy, directly to the people is the way," the SpaceX and Tesla CEO wrote in an X post. Earlier this year, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell and her husband also pledged a share of their SpaceX stock to each of more than 2 million children under the [USN:L6N43429H TEXT:"Trump Accounts investment initiative"]. MACKENZIE SCOTT'S PLEDGE MacKenzie Scott received about 4% of Amazon's stock in her 2019 divorce from the company's founder Jeff Bezos, a stake then worth about $36 billion. She signed the Giving Pledge shortly after committing to giving away at least half of her Amazon fortune during her lifetime. The Giving Pledge was founded by Buffett and Bill and Melinda Gates to encourage the world's wealthiest people to donate the majority of their fortunes. Since then, she has [USN:L2N2VQ1JR TEXT:"donated"] $275 million to Planned Parenthood (in 2022), more than $4 billion to food banks and emergency relief funds [USN:L3N2NX410 TEXT:"during"] the coronavirus pandemic, and billions of dollars in grants to causes such as racial equality, LGBTQ rights and climate change. Scott gave away $7.1 billion in 2025, according to a Yield Giving letter published last year. FORD FOUNDATION Established by Henry Ford's son Edsel in 1936 with an initial gift of $25,000, the Ford Foundation grew from a family-backed Michigan philanthropy into one of the world's largest foundations. Its current endowment is valued at about $18 billion. The 90-year-old foundation awarded $768 million through 2,288 grants in 2024. Its work is aimed at reducing poverty and injustice, strengthening democratic values and promoting international cooperation. In 2015, it launched BUILD, a five-year, $1 billion investment in the long-term capacity and sustainability of 350 social justice organizations addressing inequality around the world. The foundation renewed BUILD in 2021 with an additional $1 billion. LILLY ENDOWMENT Established in 1937 by J.K. Lilly and his sons through gifts of stock in the family drugmaker, the Lilly Endowment began with a donation of 17,500 shares valued at $262,500. Over its first 88 years, the endowment disbursed nearly $21.3 billion in grants to 11,651 charitable organizations. It paid out $3.85 billion in grants in 2025 while its assets rose to nearly $106 billion. The Indianapolis-based foundation focuses on education, community development and religion, with a particular commitment to Indiana. NOVO NORDISK FOUNDATION Established in Denmark, the Novo Nordisk Foundation traces its origins to August Krogh, H.C. Hagedorn and August Kongsted, who used profits from insulin production to support scientific and humanitarian work. The present foundation took shape in 1989, when the foundations associated with Nordisk and Novo were combined following the merger that created Novo Nordisk. It awarded a record DKK 11.8 billion ($1.77 billion), or about €1.6 billion, across 2,206 grants and philanthropic investments in 2025, up from DKK 10.1 billion in 2024. Its funding primarily supports research and initiatives spanning human health, infectious and cardiometabolic diseases, the green transition and sustainable agriculture. ($1 = 6.6526 Danish crowns)

item.title: UE presenta una nueva estrategia para el Ártico centrada en la seguridad
item.description: La Unión Europea presentó el martes una nueva estrategia para el Ártico que refleja la importancia de la región para la seguridad, con compromisos para potenciar la vigilancia por satélite, aumentar el control de los cables submarinos y ayudar a los Estados miembros a adquirir rompehielos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Unión Europea presentó el martes una nueva estrategia para el Ártico que refleja la importancia de la región para la seguridad, con compromisos para potenciar la vigilancia por satélite, aumentar el control de los cables submarinos y ayudar a los Estados miembros a adquirir rompehielos. El Ártico suscita un interés cada vez mayor entre las grandes potencias como Estados Unidos, Rusia, China y Europa, a medida que el deshielo abre nuevas rutas marítimas. El presidente estadounidense Donald Trump intentó adquirir Groenlandia, un territorio de Dinamarca, Estado miembro de la UE, mientras que las tensiones entre las naciones árticas y Rusia han aumentado desde la invasión de Ucrania por parte de Moscú en 2022. "El Ártico es un lugar donde chocan las placas tectónicas de la geopolítica", afirmó Ursula von der Leyen, presidenta de la Comisión Europea, el órgano ejecutivo de la UE. "Cuando vemos que la soberanía, la integridad territorial y las normas que han sustentado la estabilidad en la región ya no pueden darse por sentadas, tenemos que actuar", declaró a periodistas en Estrasburgo. Funcionarios de la UE afirman que Moscú ha reabierto y modernizado en los últimos años bases militares de la era soviética en la región ártica y señalaron que Rusia cuenta con una gran concentración de armas nucleares en la península de Kola, dentro del círculo polar ártico. Afirman que el Ártico se ha convertido también en un campo de pruebas para los misiles rusos. Rusia, por su parte, ha acusado a la OTAN de impulsar la militarización de la región. El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores, Serguéi Lavrov, declaró en agosto que Rusia pretendía preservar la paz y la estabilidad y reducir las amenazas a la seguridad nacional en la región.
